title: Why AI makes things up
teaser: Confident is not the same as correct

basics.say: Time for an important warning. Sometimes AI gives an answer that sounds perfect – and is completely made up.
Ask about a marathon on Mars in 1987 and it might hand you a winner's name and a finishing time.
Remember the next-word game? The model predicts what sounds right. Sounding right and being true are not the same thing.
Experts call this a hallucination. It's more likely with rare facts, exact numbers, quotes, links and recent events.
So treat answers like a smart colleague's first draft: useful, but worth checking before you rely on it.

deeper.say: It isn't lying – it isn't trying to deceive you. It fills gaps with the most plausible continuation.
You can lower the risk: give it the source document, ask it to quote from it, and tell it that 'I don't know' is fine.
Tools help too. When an assistant can search or read your files, it can base its answer on real sources – so check those sources.
For anything that matters – figures, legal points, client facts – verify with a trusted source. You stay responsible for what you share.

takeaway: AI can sound confident and still be wrong – always check what matters.
